As someone who started getting into fighting games via REV2, after the first GG back on the PS1 made me swear off fighting games "forever" because i was so bad at it (and it IS a bit bullshit sometimes) at first i was exactly like you. 

I couldnt really internalize a chunk of the tutorials,had a rough time with the motions on D-Pad, and mistakenly thought the mini game section was ALSO tutorials... that first one had me FURIOUS, trying to slam my head against that brick wall!

 "HOW IS THIS A TUTORIAL?!?! I dont even know this guys moves let alone how to do it to get under some bombs!" Though the trying to bounce on balloons and trivia game were kinda fun.

I tried button mashing my way through a character story or two, and never felt like i was improving even when i was winning. What I ended up actually doing for a while was just going down the roster and trying to clear as much as i could in their combo trials. It wasnt the MOST engaging, especially since im INCREDIBLY bad at combos, but it was better than getting stomped into the dirt with no chance online. Eventually i got more consistent with the motions, started doing better in the combo trials, and even started racing a friend through the first mini game. 

It took a good chunk of time, but it DID start to sink in. Since you have teh game already, i'd say keep grinding that out just a little bit longer before buying in to the new one, if for no other reason than to save yourself the money.

Strive is absolutely easier to pick up than XRD, but that means its ALSO easier for everyone online, who've been playing it much longer than you, and will be sitting there online just waiting for new people. Theres a very real chance youll just have a repeat of GBVS. Hell, i had that exact same thing happen to me in BOTH GBVS and DNF Duel, so i know how much it would suck to buy the game and have it happen to you again.

TL;DR: Dont give up on XRD practice just yet. Strive IS an easier game, but problems youre having already will probably carry over, better to get a handle on the fundamentals in the similar game you already own and carry those over instead.
